segments.title: Chương 200: 0200【Sáng sớm đi nhặt phân】
segments.content:
Chapter 203: Getting Up Early to Collect Manure

"On a certain day of a certain month in 2005, a bizarre murder occurred in a certain city. A masked knight, in full view of the public, killed a certain Mr. Wang, the general manager of the Ring-Within-A-Ring Entertainment City..."

"ManShen Brand Hair Gel, great results!"

"Hahahaha!"

Dorm 404.

Bursts of laughter would erupt from time to time.

The same scene had occurred frequently over the past few days.

Whenever a dorm room had a computer, it would attract a crowd of students, all gathered around watching videos boisterously.

In reality, "The Bloody Case of the Steamed Bun" was primarily spreading through downloads and file sharing. BT, Thunder, eMule, and FlashGet were the true media behind its nationwide explosion.

The number of people who watched "The Steamed Bun" on Tudou.com or 56.com probably accounted for less than 1% of the total audience.

But this was already enough to cause a massive increase in Tudou.com's user base.

"Hu Ge is such a genius!" marveled Yuan Zhen, a younger student from the dorm next door.

Someone else asked, "How do you make this kind of video?"

"Video editing software. The editing itself is actually simple. The genius of 'The Steamed Bun' lies in its script and sound effects. Especially the sound effects, Hu Ge is definitely a professional."

"I want to make parody videos too. This is hilarious!"

Deng Chen from the dorm across the hall had chosen law as his elective in his freshman year.

He raised a question, "Besides using promotional materials from 'The Promise', 'The Steamed Bun' also contains some content from the actual movie. This content must have come from pirated downloads. Could he get sued by Chen Kaige?"

"He'll probably get sued," Chen Guiliang said.

At this, the students immediately started discussing.

"Do you guys think the lawsuit against PetroChina can win?"

"Bro, the court already refused to hear the case."

"Even if they won't hear it, it's enough for the law school's faculty and students to write a few papers on."

"What are you guys talking about?"

"You don't know? Three of our Peking University professors and three graduate students are suing a subsidiary of PetroChina, demanding 10 billion yuan in compensation for the pollution of the Songhua River!"

"10 billion yuan?"

This matter was currently even more of a hot topic at Peking University than "The Bloody Case of the Steamed Bun."

It started in the middle of last month when a workshop at a PetroChina subsidiary exploded and caught fire, causing 100 tons of benzene pollutants to enter the Songhua River. At the beginning of this month, the Peking University faculty and students filed an environmental civil public interest lawsuit, demanding 10 billion yuan from PetroChina to clean up the Songhua River.

The court refused to hear the case, the reason being that "the case is unrelated to the several plaintiffs, and does not fall within the court's scope of受理."

In reality, Chen Kaige's future lawsuit against "The Steamed Bun" for copyright infringement was the same as the Peking University faculty and students' lawsuit against PetroChina now. In both cases, the relevant laws were ambiguous, and the courts directly refused to file the case!

It was almost time for dinner, so Chen Guiliang went to the cafeteria with everyone.

As they left, his roommate Li Heng was still using BT to download Ulead VideoStudio—he also wanted to make a parody video.

And Li Heng had his sights set on "A Chinese Tall Story."

Walking on the campus paths, there was a noticeable increase in students holding mobile phones.

This was especially true for students who had just bought new phones over the Christmas period. Many of them were still in the excited phase of owning their first-ever mobile phone. Even if they weren't making calls or sending texts, they couldn't help but pull them out to play a game of Snake.

Over the last two months, mobile phone prices had plummeted again!

This was already the third major price drop for phones this year.

Because additional mobile phone licenses had been issued at the beginning of the year, companies like Huawei, ZTE, Skyworth, and Changhong had all swarmed into the market, bringing the number of phone brands approved for network access in mainland China to several dozen. Not to mention the intense competition among legitimate phones, there were also a large number of unlicensed "black phones."

"Chen Guiliang!"

Someone called out to him from the path.

Chen Guiliang turned around. The person looked a little familiar, but he didn't know him.

The person said happily, "This is my new phone, just bought it today. Should I give you a call?"

"Sure," Chen Guiliang nodded.

He soon received a call. Feeling too embarrassed to ask for the person's name, Chen Guiliang saved the contact as "Peking University Classmate No. 87."

Seeing that the person had the same phone model as him, Jiang Junlai couldn't help but ask, "How much did you buy it for?"

"There's a promotion recently, only 525," the student said.

Jiang Junlai couldn't help but swear, "Damn! I bought the exact same phone for over 2300 last year."

"Hahaha!"

Hearing this made that student feel even better.

The group strolled to the first cafeteria, each picking a window to queue up for food.

Because the rice in this cafeteria was too hard, Chen Guiliang had now gotten used to eating noodles and other wheat-based foods.

Two guys quickly finished their meals and rushed off to the weekly ballroom dance event, fantasizing about meeting pretty girls.

"Hey, Mr. Chen!"

Two girls walked past together, waving and laughing at Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang smiled and nodded in return. He found them somewhat familiar too but didn't know their names.

The cafeteria was playing a highlight reel of the NBA Christmas Day games, and many male students were staring at the TV as they ate.

The commentator, Zhang Weiping, spoke in his iconic tone, "Kobe has the ball, Wade is on him... a crossover! A sudden stop! A fadeaway jumper—what a shot! That was a really tough one. Wade's defense was right on his fingertips, but Kobe can still sink it! That's a superstar for you!"

"Shaq is posting up... Divac can't hold him at all! He catches the ball, turns... bang! A two-handed power dunk, and he draws the foul... that dunk was carrying a year's worth of resentment!"

"What a play!"

Some male students in the cafeteria even stood up in excitement.

Like the other guys, Chen Guiliang was captivated by the highlight reel.

Sigh, twenty years from now, you probably wouldn't see a scene like this anymore.

The NBA's own doing.

After the highlights finished, Chen Guiliang suddenly felt like playing basketball.

Not today, though.

He'd ask Xie Yang, Yang Shuo, and Crazy Guo to play together some other day.

On the way back to the dorm, the group was still chatting about the NBA.

"I'm gonna shatter the backboard!"

Jiang Junlai stood on a raised flower bed, mimicked Shaq's posture from earlier, and jumped down for a "dunk." He lost his footing on landing and fell face-first onto the ground.

"Hahaha!"

Everyone burst out laughing.

Another classmate ran over to tease him, faking a dribbling motion and wiggling in front of him.

"Get lost, get lost!" Jiang Junlai said irritably.

Laughing and fooling around, they returned to their dorm building. Some students grabbed their thermoses to get hot water.

Chen Guiliang took out the excerpts from "History of Ming" and "Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty" that he had copied down some time ago to organize his ideas for the last few tens of thousands of words of the fourth volume of "Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty."

Last year, he had written the first three volumes in just half a year.

This year, a whole year had passed, and he still hadn't finished the fourth volume... Li Xunhuan was about ready to curse him out.

After some unknown amount of time, Li Heng finished downloading VideoStudio and began staring at online tutorials to learn how to edit videos. He turned his head and asked, "Senior Chen, do you need to use the computer?"

"Not for a while," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Heng asked, "How do you think I should parody 'A Chinese Tall Story'?"

"That movie is already a nonsensical parody itself," Chen Guiliang said. "No matter how brilliantly you parody it, you'll never achieve the same effect as 'The Steamed Bun'. You have to pick your target for a parody. It's only by parodying a dead-serious film like 'The Promise' that you can create that contrasting effect."

"That's true. It's the contrast that makes it work," Li Heng nodded.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What are some of the more serious videos on Tudou.com right now?"

Li Heng replied, "They're all just some..."
